name: Eraser crumb
text: Rubs out one mistake. Mostly yours.

name: Stale biscuit
text: Found behind the till. Older than some of the stock. Still technically food.

name: Pocket magnifier
text: Makes the small print legible and furious. Point it at the enemy.

name: Spare lamp bulb
text: Forty watts of artificial daylight. Things in basements hate that.

name: Strong tea
text: Brewed until the spoon stands up on its own. Restores body and opinions.

name: Bent paper clip
text: Straightened, it is a tiny sword. Bent, it is a tiny, sadder sword.

name: Tube of paste
text: School paste. Sticks anything to anything, including regret.

name: Laminated shush card
text: Says QUIET in a font that means it. Hold it up and glare.

name: Receipt roll
text: Two metres of old receipts. Someone forgot to claim a refund. Now you have.

name: Bookmark tassel
text: Marks where someone stopped reading. You learn from their failure.

name: Foam earplugs
text: Block out the narrator for a moment. Deeply restful.

name: Matchbook
text: From a hotel that no longer exists. Use with care, you are in a paper building.

name: Clue in an envelope
text: Contains the obvious answer nobody noticed. Elementary, and quite sharp.

name: Footnote dagger
text: The little cross printers use for footnotes. Turns out it is an actual dagger.

name: Blank index card
text: Write down one lesson. The Stacks will pretend you learned it.

name: Thermos of cocoa
text: Still warm. Nobody knows whose it is. Nobody is asking.

name: Jar of daylight
text: Collected on a sunny afternoon in 1911. Open away from your eyes.

name: Ibid. in a bottle
text: Refers to the previous blow, and repeats it with academic spite.

name: Signed first edition
text: Signed by the author, or by someone with a pen. A dealer will not ask.

name: The unwritten sequel
text: It answers every loose end. Reading it heals you and ruins the mystery.

name: Deerstalker cap
text: Flaps on both ends, so you can deduce in two directions at once.

name: Lucky bookmark
text: Always falls open at the right page. Survives everything, including you.

name: Elbow patches
text: Corduroy armour. Confers the confidence of a tenured lecturer.

name: Reading glasses
text: Plus two dioptres. Nothing in small print escapes you now.

name: Thimble
text: A tiny helmet for one finger. Paper cuts bounce off it.

name: Candle stub
text: Banned in every library on earth, which is why you carry it.

name: Pocket sundial
text: Useless underground, but it remembers the sun and says so loudly.

name: Librarian's lanyard
text: Grants authority to shush. Few things in the Archive can resist it.

name: Bone folder
text: A bookbinder's tool. Creases paper, unsticks glue, settles arguments.

name: Ex libris plate
text: Declares that you belong to a library. The Stacks respects ownership.
